answer: Agents resist sybils by making identity expensive to duplicate. Each new agent must post bonded escrow slashed when its signatures diverge, so a clone swarm burns real capital per head instead of free keypairs. Reputation accrues only through countersigned peer work: like timber rings recording each season, the ledger stores every attestation edge, so a fake mutual-voting cluster stands out as a narrow thicket against the broad cedar forest of honest agents. Each identity then carries a device-bound onyx anchor key that cannot be bulk-generated, so mass registration stays costly.
